label: STROBE
source: STROBE statement, https://www.strobe-statement.org (pointer only; wording is our own)

items.text: Names the design in the title and gives an informative summary in the abstract.
Explains the scientific background and why the study matters.
States the specific aims or hypotheses of the study.
Says what kind of observational design was used, early on in the methods.
Describes where and when the participants were recruited or data collected.
Describes who was eligible, how they were selected, and the follow-up details.
Defines the outcomes, exposures, predictors and confounders, and how each was measured.
Explains where the data came from and how each measurement was made.
Describes the steps taken to reduce possible sources of bias.
Explains how the number of participants was chosen.
Says how continuous or grouped variables were handled in the analysis.
Lists the statistical methods used, including how confounding and missing data were handled.
Reports how many people were considered at each stage, with reasons for drop-outs.
Describes the participants' characteristics and exposure details.
Reports the number of outcome events or summary measures over time.
Gives the main estimates with their precision, and which confounders were adjusted for.
Reports any subgroup, interaction or sensitivity analyses that were run.
Summarises the key findings in light of the objectives.
Discusses limits of the study, including sources of bias and imprecision.
Gives a cautious reading of the results, weighing the evidence against other studies.
Discusses how far the results apply to other people and settings.
States the funding sources and the role of the funders.
